text:
NEEDS_FIX: YES
<assessment>The source collage shows a tall glazed A-frame café hall with exposed timber roof framing, a lower rectangular café volume, a sloped glazed front annex, an elevated terrace and access stair. The exterior panels also show a separate upper canopy over terrace seating, while the lower terrace slab/fascia projects over an open bay carried by columns. The interior panel confirms the repeated timber roof structure and tall glazed gable. These main forms and both canopy levels are present in the current views, and the lower bay remains open between its supports. However, the current close canopy view shows the upper canopy obscuring more of the glazed roof than in the source, and the current side wall reads as broad smooth peach panels rather than the source’s timber panel cladding.</assessment>
<issue priority="1" view="roof">problem: The upper terrace canopy projects across and obscures the glazed A-frame roof in the current close view, weakening the source’s separation between the roof hall and terrace seating. action: Reduce its projection or shift it toward the terrace seating edge, keeping it distinct from the lower terrace fascia and supported on its own posts.</issue>
<issue priority="2" view="right">problem: The large side wall has widely spaced seams and a smooth peach finish; the source shows a warmer timber-clad surface with a finer, regular vertical panel rhythm. action: Refine the existing wall finish with narrow vertical timber joints and shallow panel relief, preserving the wall’s current footprint and openings.</issue>
<keep>Glazed A-frame hall and its exposed timber roof grid.</keep>
<keep>Sloped glazed front annex descending to the ground.</keep>
<keep>Lower projecting fascia and its open, column-supported seating bay.</keep>
